basicInfo.description: Pycytominer is a toolkit for processing high dimensional readouts from high-throughput image-based profiling experiments.

_curatorNote: Submitter (the tool's own point of contact) entered developerName/developerAffiliation as 'Many' — Pycytominer is a multi-contributor open-source package (github.com/cytomining/pycytominer), not single-developer. Set developerName to Gregory Way as the identifiable point-of-contact/investigator (Synapse: @gwaybio, ownerId 3328264) pending curator confirmation of the intended primary investigator. The registry's investigator pipeline (upsert_publication_links.py: upsert_investigators) already splits a semicolon-separated developerName ('Alice; Bob') into multiple Investigator rows (syn26486833) each linked to this resource via the dev-links table (syn26486807) — so multiple named developers ARE supported if a curator wants to list specific co-developers instead of 'Many'. Checked existing submissions/VALIDATED_*.csv for other tools by Gregory Way or the Way Lab (e.g. CellProfiler, DeepProfiler, CytoTable) to cross-link this investigator — none found yet; Pycytominer would be the first tool in the registry linked to this investigator. Per reviewer suggestion, also checked Synapse for studies/datasets tied to @gwaybio: he is a studyLead (with Alice Soragni, Sara Gosline) on syn62031004 'A deep learning microscopy framework for NF1 patient-derived organoid drug screening' (GFF-funded, Next Generation Models initiative, dataType includes 'morphology parameter') — a strong candidate usage link for Pycytominer (image-based morphological profiling) once that study starts using/citing it; not yet added as a usage link since no citing publication/DOI confirms it does.
